title: GBX Professional Services, 30-second brand commercial, six 5-second clips
how_to_use: Six clips, one per beat, each 5 seconds. Clips 1 to 5 are text to video on Seedance 2.5. Clip 6 is NOT generated: it is the site's own animated mark, public/media/logo-animation.mp4 (5.04 seconds, 624 square, H.264), placed as the final clip in the edit with the voiceover over it and the closing line and URL added as a text overlay from docs/gbx-endcard-1920.png. On-screen text inside the AI clips has been removed on purpose: the 'Super, explained.' slide title and the 'Education, not advice.' lower third are added in the edit, which removes the spelling risk entirely. Generate clips 1 to 5 at 480p to check, then 1080p for the final, and assemble with a 0.3 second cross-fade between clips.

voice.direction: One male voiceover across all six clips: mature, in his sixties, warm and unhurried, friendly with a wry edge, the wisdom of someone who has seen a few cycles and is still curious about new technology. Measured baritone, precise diction, neutral accent with a light Australian and New Zealand lean. Sounds like a trusted mentor explaining something over a coffee, not a presenter. No sales energy, no echo, natural pauses.
voice.consistency_note: Each clip generates its own voice, so the six reads will differ slightly. For a broadcast-quality result, generate the voiceover once as a single track (an AI voice service or a session with a real voice actor using the direction above) and lay it over the clips in the edit, generating every clip as picture only or with ambience only. The drafts keep the voice in each clip so you can judge the direction.
voice.avoid: Do not name a real actor or public figure in the prompt. OpenArt models do not reproduce a specific person's voice or likeness, and a request to imitate one can be refused. The description above gets the same feel.

shared_style: Cinematic brand film, editorial and premium. Dark charcoal and deep teal palette with warm off-white highlights, fine film grain, soft directional light, shallow depth of field, slow deliberate camera movement. Real-feeling Australian professionals in their thirties to fifties, diverse, natural and unposed, in a modern Melbourne office with the city skyline through glass. No stock-photo smiles, no pointing at screens, no logos, no text of any kind on screen. Minimal music: a low ambient pad with a soft piano motif, quiet room tone. Voice always clear above the music.

params.prompt: SHARED_STYLE. Dawn over the Melbourne skyline seen from a high office window, the city still quiet, first light arriving on the glass. One slow push-in toward an empty desk by the window with a closed notebook and a cup of coffee. No people, no text. VOICE_DIRECTION. The voiceover is spoken slowly and evenly across the full seven seconds, with a beat of quiet before the first word and a beat after the last, every word completed, never rushed or cut off. VOICEOVER: "Most businesses don't need more advice. They need a clearer picture."

SHARED_STYLE. One continuous shot, one scene, no cuts. Soft morning light. A woman in her forties and a man in his fifties stand together at a whiteboard in an open office, working through a simple process flow of boxes and arrows drawn in black marker, no readable words. He draws one more arrow while she talks it through with him; they are clearly in conversation with each other, glancing between the board and one another, nodding. A third colleague sits at a nearby desk, half out of focus, listening in. The camera drifts slowly sideways around them. Nobody looks at the camera; nobody speaks aloud, only the narrator is heard. VOICE_DIRECTION. The narration is spoken slowly and evenly across the full seven seconds, with a beat of quiet before the first word and a beat after the last, every word completed, never rushed or cut off. NARRATOR, off screen: "GBX Professional Services helps firms run sharper. The numbers, the process, the pipeline."

clips.name: The hours given back

params.prompt: SHARED_STYLE. One continuous shot, one scene, no cuts. Dusk, the city lights just coming on through the glass. A man in his fifties at his desk slides a thick folder of paperwork to one side, closes his laptop with one hand, a plain matte charcoal lid with no logo and no display on it, the soft teal glow of its screen fading as it shuts. He stands, lifts his coat from the back of the chair, and walks out of frame past two colleagues still working at their desks, unhurried, a small satisfied breath, nobody looking at the camera. The camera holds on the tidy desk and the skyline as he goes. VOICE_DIRECTION. Nobody on screen speaks. The narration is spoken slowly and evenly across the full seven seconds, with a beat of quiet before the first word and a beat after the last, every word completed, never rushed or cut off. NARRATOR, off screen: "And AI that actually earns its keep. Practical, governed, and only where it helps."

clips.idea: AI earning its keep is shown as the payoff, not the tool: the work is done and he leaves on time while others are still at it.

clips.name: Teaching money plainly (boardroom, silent picture plus narration)
clips.mode: text2video, picture only, then narration muxed in

params.prompt: SHARED_STYLE (but the one slide below may carry text). Silent film, no dialogue, no narration. Documentary feel, nobody looks at the camera. A modern corporate boardroom in a Melbourne office, long timber table, twelve staff of all ages seated along it in relaxed working clothes, seen in profile and from behind, all facing a relaxed presenter in his sixties who stands at the far end beside a wall screen. The wall screen shows a plain soft teal slide with only one line of clean white sans-serif text, large and centred, reading exactly: Tax basics for employees. No other text, numbers or logos anywhere. The presenter is quietly talking to the room in the background, his lips moving naturally as he explains something, gesturing with one open hand, easy and unhurried. Camera tracks slowly along the side of the table past the backs and profiles of listeners: one takes a note, one leans back and nods slightly, one turns to a colleague with a small smile. Natural, attentive, warm.

clips.voiceover: We also teach people about money. Plainly, at work, in language a whole team can follow.
clips.audio: Generate the picture with generateAudio false. Take the narration from a separate take (any clip carrying this line, or the single 30-second voice track) and mux it on: ffmpeg -i picture.mp4 -i narration.mp4 -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -c:v copy -c:a aac -shortest clip4.mp4. Seedance lip-syncs any voice it generates to whoever is visible speaking, so a talking presenter and a narrator cannot share one generation.

clips.name: Free tools, then the Diagnostic
clips.mode: screen capture of the live site, not generated
clips.how_it_was_made: scripts/record-tools-clip.mjs drives headless Chromium over the built site at 1920x1080, takes one screenshot per frame at 24fps (7.25 seconds, paced so nothing rushes), then ffmpeg assembles the frames into H.264. Re-run it after any Tools & Insights redesign so the clip matches the live site.
shot_list: 0.0s to 0.6s: Tools & Insights hero, cursor resting top right.
0.6s to 2.1s: smooth scroll down to the tool card grid, short hold.
2.5s to 4.3s: second scroll to the next row of cards, cursor glides to Business Health Check and clicks Start the check.
4.8s to 7.25s: Business Health Check opens, cursor answers the first two questions, hold on step three.
clips.audio: The capture has no audio. Lay the voice-over and the shared music bed over it in the edit.
clips.voiceover: Free tools before you ever hire us. A ten-day Diagnostic when you're ready.
clips.regenerate: node scripts/record-tools-clip.mjs (see the header comment in that file for the preview server, fonts and ffmpeg steps).

clips.name: End card: the mark, the philosophy, the address, then the site
clips.mode: screen capture of the live site, not generated
clips.how_it_was_made: scripts/record-endcard-clip.mjs plays the real logo animation (public/media/logo-animation.mp4, frame by frame at 24fps) alone on black, then eases it upward while the philosophy line from the home page fades in beneath it, then www.gbxps.com, then a capture of the live home page (header and hero) fades up into the bottom of the frame. 7.5 seconds, 1920x1080, no audio.
shot_list: 0.0s to 3.4s: the animated GBX mark alone, centred on black, building to the full mark.
3.4s to 4.6s: the mark eases up and shrinks a little.
3.9s to 4.9s: OUR PHILOSOPHY and the line Combining insight with impact for sustainable business growth fade in beneath the mark, in the site's serif italic.
5.1s to 5.9s: www.gbxps.com fades in below the line.
5.4s to 6.8s: the home page rises and fades in along the bottom edge, showing the header and the top of the hero.
clips.audio: The capture has no audio. Lay the voice-over over it and let the music resolve on a single warm swell, then silence for the last half second.
clips.voiceover: Three leaders. One operating view. GBX Professional Services.
clips.regenerate: node scripts/record-endcard-clip.mjs (see the header comment in that file). Re-run after any home hero change.

placeholders.SHARED_STYLE: Replace with the shared_style paragraph above.
placeholders.VOICE_DIRECTION: Replace with the voice.direction paragraph above.

edit_notes: Order the clips 1 to 6 with a 0.3 second cross-fade; six clips of about seven seconds run to roughly 42 seconds with the fades. For a strict 30-second slot, trim the tail of clips 1 to 4 after the last word rather than speeding anything up.
Clip 5 is a real screen capture, so grade it lightly to sit with the generated clips (a touch of the same warm contrast) and keep the cursor visible; do not crop off the header.
Add the lower third 'Education, not advice.' over clip 4 in the site's off-white sans-serif, small, bottom left.
Music: lay one continuous ambient track under all six clips rather than using each clip's own music, so the bed does not jump at the cuts.
Log the finished cut in docs/content-review-log.md before publishing.

assets.end_card_reference: docs/gbx-endcard-1920.png (1920 by 1080, the real mark from public/media/logo-poster.jpg with the closing line and URL in the site's fonts)
assets.animated_mark: public/media/logo-animation.mp4, with public/media/logo-loop.gif and public/media/logo-poster.jpg as fallbacks
assets.note: No generated logo is used anywhere in the spot. Clips 1 to 5 contain no logos or text by instruction.

lessons_from_the_drafts: Any visible screen, slide or paper invites made-up lettering. Turn screens away, blur them, or keep them as a plain gradient.
Rooms of people facing the camera read as a group photo. Ask for profiles and backs, a tracking move, and 'nobody looks at the camera'.
Five-second clips cut words off. Seven seconds with 'a beat of quiet before the first word and after the last' gives the read room without the model drifting off script.
Generated laptop and phone screens always render gibberish text. Anything that must show the product is a real screen capture, not a generation.
Even with 'no text' in the prompt, dashboards and whiteboards still grow tiny labels. At 480p they are unreadable; check them again at 1080p before the final render.
When a person on screen is meant to be talking, say so and say their voice is never heard, and label the read NARRATOR, off screen. Otherwise the model lip-syncs the voice-over to whoever is visible.
Two half-scenes in one prompt come out disjointed. Ask for one continuous shot, one scene, no cuts, and describe the people as in conversation with each other.
A laptop facing the camera grows a screen on its lid. Say the lid is plain, matte, with no display on it, and the screen faces the person.
A single short line of on-screen text (Tax basics for employees) rendered correctly at 7 seconds when asked for exactly that text, large, centred, and nothing else on the slide.

If someone on screen is meant to be talking, the model lip-syncs the narration to them no matter what the prompt says. Generate that clip as picture only (generateAudio false) and mux the narration on afterwards with ffmpeg.
Abstract props (cards in slots) read as nonsense. Show the outcome people recognise instead: for AI, the work done and someone leaving on time.
